law: You may not stand or park a vehicle within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
question: How far from a fire hydrant must you park?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1003(m) — 'A person may not stand or park a vehicle within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.'

law: Except in Baltimore City, you may not stand or park a vehicle within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.
question: How far from a crosswalk at an intersection must you park?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1003(n) — 'A person may not stand or park a vehicle within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.'

law: You may not stop, stand or park a vehicle in an intersection.
question: May you park in an intersection?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1003(d) — 'A person may not stop, stand, or park a vehicle in an intersection.'

law: You may not stand or park a vehicle within 30 feet on the approach to a flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign or traffic signal at the side of the road.
question: How far from a stop sign or traffic signal must you park?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1003(o) — 'A person may not stand or park a vehicle within 30 feet on the approach to any flashing signal, stop sign, yield sign, or traffic control signal located at the side of a roadway.'

law: You may not stand or park within 20 feet of a fire station driveway, or within 75 feet of it on the opposite side of the road where signs say so.
question: How far from a fire station driveway must you park?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1003(p) — 'A person may not stand or park a vehicle within 20 feet of the driveway entrance to any fire station or on the side of a highway opposite the entrance to any fire station within 75 feet of the entrance, if properly signposted.'

law: You may not park a vehicle within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.
question: How far from a railroad crossing must you park?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1003(t) — 'A person may not park a vehicle within 50 feet of the nearest rail in a railroad grade crossing.'

law: On a two-way road you must park parallel to the right-hand curb, with your right-hand wheels within 12 inches of it.
question: How close to the curb must you park?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1004(a) — 'a vehicle that is stopped or parked on a two-way roadway shall be stopped or parked parallel to the right hand curb or edge of the roadway, with its right hand wheels within 12 inches of that curb or edge of the roadway.'

law: Unless on official business, you may not follow within 500 feet of a fire truck answering an alarm, or drive or park within 300 feet of one stopped at an alarm.
question: How far behind a fire truck answering an alarm may you follow?
citation:
Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1109(a) — '(1) Follow within 500 feet of any fire apparatus traveling in response to a fire alarm; or
(2) Drive or park within 300 feet of any fire apparatus stopped in response to a fire alarm.'

law: A signal to turn right or left must be given continuously for at least the last 100 feet before the turn.
question: How far before a turn must you signal?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-604(d) — 'a signal of intention to turn right or left shall be given continuously during at least the last 100 feet traveled by the vehicle before turning'

law: Where no other limit is set, the maximum speed is 30 mph on all highways in a business district and on undivided highways in a residential district, and 35 mph on divided highways in a residential district.
question: What is the speed limit on a residential street when no sign is posted?
citation:
Md. Code, Transp. § 21-801.1(b) — '(2) 30 miles per hour on:
(i) All highways in a business district; and
(ii) Undivided highways in a residential district;
(3) 35 miles per hour on divided highways in a residential district;'

law: Where no other limit is set, the maximum speed elsewhere is 50 mph on undivided highways and 55 mph on divided highways.
question: What is the speed limit on a highway outside town when no sign is posted?
citation:
Md. Code, Transp. § 21-801.1(b) — '(4) 50 miles per hour on undivided highways in other locations; and
(5) 55 miles per hour on divided highways in other locations.'

law: Every licensee under 21 is under an alcohol restriction: no driving with any alcohol in the blood at all.
question: What is the blood alcohol limit for drivers under 21?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 16-113(b) — 'the Administration shall impose on each licensee under the age of 21 years an alcohol restriction that prohibits the licensee from driving or attempting to drive a motor vehicle while having alcohol in the licensee’s blood.'

law: You may not drive while wearing earphones attached to a radio or other audio device over or in both ears.
question: May you wear headphones while driving?
citation: Md. Code, Transp. § 21-1120(c) — 'while the person is wearing over or in both ears earphones attached to a radio, tape player, or other audio device.'

law: No one in a vehicle on a highway may have an open container holding any amount of alcohol in the passenger area.
question: May you have an open container of alcohol in the car?
citation: Md. Code, Crim. Law § 10-125(a) — 'an occupant of a motor vehicle may not possess an open container that contains any amount of an alcoholic beverage in a passenger area of a motor vehicle on a highway.'

law: Littering up to 100 pounds, not for gain, is a misdemeanor with up to 30 days in jail or a fine of up to $1,500, or both.
question: What is the penalty for littering?
citation: Md. Code, Crim. Law § 10-110(f) — 'is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction is subject to imprisonment not exceeding 30 days or a fine not exceeding $1,500 or both.'
